xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5623: Reclaim Overdeck-owned workspace stack containers of parked issues while the gate admission queue is starved (FR-2 of #5621)

plan.title: Reclaim Overdeck-owned workspace stack containers of parked issues while the gate admission queue is starved (FR-2 of #5621)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: The plan touches 30 files across 6 subsystems (src/lib, src/dashboard, src/cli, tests/unit, docs/PIPELINE-GATES.md, changelog.d/pan-5623.md). Stopping stacks, journaling the stop, making the journal-tail readers skip the new entries and starting the stacks again are inseparable: a reclaim without the restore path strands stopped containers under live agents, a restore path with nothing reclaiming is dead code, and the new journal entries without the tail-reader skip would hide blocked.declared and failed-dispatch tails from the board and deacon recoveries. 11 of the 30 files are tests, and PAN-5621 already took the separable detection half.

narratives.Problem: While the quality-gate admission queue is starved on memory (PAN-5621 detects and reports it), parked issues' workspace stacks (api/fe/frontend/server containers) keep holding memory while their agents only wait. On 2026-11-23 the Flywheel had to stop four MYN containers by hand before the head gate could run. Nothing frees that memory automatically, and nothing would start a stopped stack again when its issue needs it: a parked agent woken by a message is not respawned, and stopped containers read as STACK BROKEN.
narratives.Proposal: A primary-dashboard service (src/dashboard/server/services/stack-reclaim-service.ts) polls every 30 s. While PAN-5621's starvation episode is open and the head still cannot fit alone, it picks at most one parked issue per poll (deny-by-default closed candidate list: compose-label ownership, no gate/verification activity, only idle work panes at a turn boundary, unresolved blocker or merge-gate ready), largest container memory first and at most once per episode, journals stack.reclaimed with the exact names, then docker-stops only api/fe/frontend/server. A plain-lib restore door (src/lib/workspace/stack-restore.ts) docker-starts exactly the journaled names and journals stack.restored; it runs when an issue pane starts a turn (5 s poll with a journal-seeded index), in the spawn gate before its health read, and when a verification run starts. Journal tail readers skip stack.* housekeeping entries. Display-only health reads (pan status, workspace-data) treat a journaled reclaim as stopped on purpose; gating reads stay strict.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No dashboard UI (card, badge or button) for reclaimed stacks.
- No restart when the operator opens the workspace's app in a browser (PAN-5250 owns that); the activity entry prints the manual docker start command.
- No pan workspace up verb.
- No new config key and no per-project service list.
- No change to the idle-stack reaper (idle-stack-reaper.ts) and no reuse of its listComposeContainers.
- No reclaim outside an open PAN-5621 starvation episode; no bulk restore when the episode ends.
- Never stop dev, database, cache or any service outside api/fe/frontend/server, or any container outside the issue's compose project; no docker rm, docker compose down or volume removal.
- No change to admission decisions, to PAN-5621's detection/announcement logic or to the starvation record format; do not copy or edit PAN-5621 source files (gate-starvation.ts, gate-starvation-service.ts, quality-gate-memory.ts, quality-gate-admission.ts); wi15 does edit PAN-5621's sentence in docs/PIPELINE-GATES.md.
- No use of rebuildWorkspaceStack (up -d --build) by reclaim or restore code.
- Gating health reads (spawn gate, spawn-issue route, summary-fork handoff source check) never pass reclaimAware; the spawn gate's only health change is a fresh listing after a restore.

autoDecisions.summary: Approved issues held for operator UAT are reclaimable when the merge gate says ready
autoDecisions.rationale: The incident's containers (MIN-1144, MIN-1146) were exactly such issues and the Flywheel stopped them by hand to unstick the queue; operator-open restart is PAN-5250's scope and the activity entry prints the manual docker start command.

autoDecisions.summary: Reclaimable services are the closed constant api, fe, frontend, server
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue names this allow-list; docker ps on this host (2026-11-23) shows these plus dev/postgres/redis, which must never stop.

autoDecisions.summary: Journal stack.reclaimed before running docker stop
autoDecisions.rationale: A crash between the two then leaves a record naming running containers (a later restore is a no-op), never stopped containers with no record that nothing would restart.

autoDecisions.summary: This issue owns the restart path; PAN-5250 reuses restoreReclaimedStack
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue says whichever lands first owns it, and PAN-5250 has no workspace or branch.

autoDecisions.summary: 'Approved, waiting on merge' means evaluateIssueMergeGate(...).ready, checked only for the top 3 candidates by memory
autoDecisions.rationale: The merge gate is the authority (approval at head, green checks, mergeability, CI test job, UAT policy); running it last keeps forge reads to a few per poll.

autoDecisions.summary: Container memory comes from a one-shot docker stats --no-stream on candidate names
autoDecisions.rationale: DockerStatsCollector starts lazily only when a route asks for it, so the service cannot rely on it.

autoDecisions.summary: Reclaimed-as-stopped leniency applies only to display reads (pan status, workspace-data)
autoDecisions.rationale: The spawn route calls the spawn gate only when health is unhealthy and summary-fork trusts healthy, so a lenient gating read could let a spawn proceed against stopped containers after a failed restore.

autoDecisions.summary: At most one reclaim per issue per starvation episode
autoDecisions.rationale: Prevents flapping when a woken agent's stack is restored and the agent returns to a turn boundary in the same episode.

autoDecisions.summary: Live review panes do not block a reclaim or trigger a restore
autoDecisions.rationale: Verified 2026-11-23: MIN-1144 and MIN-1146 (the incident issues, both merge-gate ready) each keep a finished review pane alive beside an idle work pane; requiring work-only panes would never have fired on the motivating case, and review never needs the stack (PAN-4690).
The reclaim acts only inside a starvation episode, whose threshold is already configurable (resources.quality_gate_starvation_minutes); the issue does not ask for a switch.

metadata.parallelSafeReason: It owns two new files (the service and its test) that no other item touches except wi13, which a blocks edge serializes after it; its inputs (wi2, wi4, wi11) are merged before it dispatches.
metadata.acJustification: Six criteria: the reclaim poll is the one item whose safety rules (trigger, candidate exclusions, re-check, confirmed journal write, stop by id, error isolation) each need their own observable check.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-12. PRECONDITION: run `git show origin/main:src/lib/cloister/gate-starvation.ts > /dev/null`; if it fails, run `pan task block pan-5623 wi12-reclaim-poll --on PAN-5621`, do the other items, and `pan sync-main` once PAN-5621 merges. Never copy PAN-5621 code. Create the service modeled on gate-starvation-service.ts with the Deps listed in the PRD and runStackReclaimPoll implementing steps 1-8 in order (record open, no close reason, head still blocked via fitsAloneAboveHardReserve, docker/pane reads non-null, FR-2 rules 1-7, memory read, rank, parked check on the top 3 with pendingDeclarations before mergeReady, then inside withFileLock(<workspace>/.overdeck/stack-reclaim.lock, timeoutMs 5_000; timeout = idle 'lock-busy') re-check from fresh reads the open episode, close reason, blocked head, rules 4, 5 and 7, and every target container's id/running state/project/service (any failure: idle 'changed-before-stop'), append stack.reclaimed (names + verified ids) BEFORE stopping, read it back with openStackReclaim (mismatch: idle 'journal-unwritable', no stop), then stopContainer(id) for each verified id, emit the D14 activity, add to the restore index). startStackReclaimService/stopStackReclaimService own both timers (restore tick a no-op until wi13), each with an in-flight guard and a catch that logs and never rethrows. Tests per PRD WI-12, all with vi.useFakeTimers().
